label: Overview
title: I redesigned how Sri Lanka orders pizza.
lead: Ordering pizza should be the easiest part of the night. Online, it often isn’t: too many steps before anything reaches the cart, prices that change at checkout, and no simple way to say “ready at 7, please”.

blocks.label: My role
blocks.text: This is my concept for the Domino’s Sri Lanka website. I led the UX and UI end to end, from the first sketches to a working, responsive prototype.

blocks.alt: Hi, I’m Kavinda. I redesigned how Sri Lanka orders pizza: an illustration of Kavinda eating pizza next to a photo of two pizzas

label: The problem
title: Hungry people don’t read instructions.
lead: I walked through a typical online pizza order step by step, like a hungry customer would. These thoughts kept coming up.

items.title: Too many steps
items.text: “I have to pick a crust before I can even add it?”

items.title: Price surprises
items.text: “Wait… why is it Rs 600 more now?”

items.title: Unclear timing
items.text: “Which store even delivers here?”

items.title: No order ahead
items.text: “Can I just order it for 7 pm?”

items.title: Add in one tap
items.text: Smart defaults on every pizza. Customise only if you want to.

items.title: No price surprises
items.text: Real prices with taxes, and the best deal applied for you.

items.title: Built for Sri Lanka
items.text: Local areas, stores, wallets and LankaQR.

items.title: Now or later
items.text: Order for right now, or book up to seven days ahead.

label: Who it’s for
title: Meet Nethmi. Hungry, and busy.
lead: A proto-persona kept every decision grounded in a real moment: ordering on a phone, between other things, often for a group.

blocks.name: Nethmi Perera
blocks.bio: “Just tell me what I’ll pay and when it’ll arrive.”

cols.title: Habits
items: Orders for the team every Friday
Pays with Genie or a card
Always on her phone, one hand busy

blocks.alt: Her ordering journey: before, the experience dips at customise, checkout and wait; after the redesign it stays happy from craving to wait

blocks.label: Note
blocks.text: Proto-persona and journey based on assumptions and a heuristic review, to be validated with real customers.

label: Real moments
title: Designed for real people, in real moments.
lead: Three everyday moments shaped every decision: the team lunch, the late night with friends, and the rider bringing it to the door.

blocks.alt: Illustrations: ordering for the whole team on a Friday lunch, sharing with friends late at night, and the rider right on time

label: Process
title: From napkin to pixels.
lead: Every screen went through the same three steps: an idea on paper, structure in grey boxes, then the flavour.

blocks.alt: The home screen as a paper sketch, a grey wireframe and the final interface

items: Sketch: quick ideas on paper. The big one: order straight from the hero.
Wireframe: grey boxes to lock the hierarchy: what, how much, one button.
Interface: brand colour, real photos, live prices and motion.

label: What I improved
title: My first version worked. It just wasn’t Domino’s.
lead: The first build was clean but generic: illustrated pizzas, a soft beige palette and the same card everywhere. I rebuilt every screen around the brand and the four goals. These are real screens from both versions.

blocks.alt: Before: the first version with illustrated pizzas on beige. After: the final design with a blue hero and real pizza photos

items.text: Design iterations between the first version and the final one.
Screens rebuilt: hero, offers, menu, customise, cart, checkout, payment and footer.

items.title: 1 rule
items.text: Every change had to make ordering faster, clearer or more trustworthy.

label: Before and after
title: From a search banner to a hero you can order from.
lead: The first hero asked people to search. The new one puts a pizza, a size and an Add button on the very first screen.

blocks.alt: Home before and after

blocks.title: Home
items: Order from the hero: a swipeable deck of featured pizzas with a size picker and one-tap Add.
Brand first: Domino’s blue, real food photos instead of illustrations, and the tile motif.
A reason to act now: today’s deal with a live countdown sits right under the headline.

blocks.alt: Most loved and deals, before and after

blocks.title: From plain lists to offers that sell
items: Photos lead: full-bleed food photography with the name and price laid over it.
Ranked, not listed: big #1, #2, #3 numbers help first-timers pick a favourite fast.
Deals you can grab: tear-off coupons with an “ends tonight” timer, applied automatically.

blocks.alt: Menu before and after: identical illustrated cards become photo-first cards

blocks.title: From identical cards to photo-first cards
items: Size on the card: a sliding size switcher, with the real price for that size.
Add without a dialog: one tap adds the pizza with sensible defaults. Customise is optional.
Filters that stay: category tabs, Veg only, Spicy and search stick while you scroll.

blocks.alt: Customise and cart, before and after

blocks.title: Less to read, more to see
items: See the size: real pizza photos that grow with the inches, instead of small icons.
Live total: the Add button always shows what you’ll pay as you choose.
Deal applied for you: the cart finds the best deal and spells out the saving. No codes.

blocks.alt: Checkout before and after

blocks.title: From “schedule for later” to real order ahead
items: Progress, not paperwork: a clean progress tracker replaces the stack of numbered cards.
Day, then time: seven days ahead, grouped by lunch to late night, with busy times marked Full.
A clear commitment: “Book order” shows the exact time and store before you pay.

blocks.alt: Footer before and after

blocks.title: From a sign-off to a brand moment
items: The promise, big: “Hot. Fresh. Yours.” with a gentle light sweep over an ingredient wall.
Still useful: track an order, call the hotline and check opening hours, right there.
Every way to pay: cards, cash, Genie, eZ Cash, FriMi and LankaQR, shown with their logos.

label: Mobile
title: On the phone, where most orders start.
lead: The same improvements, sized for one hand: bigger photos, actions within thumb reach, and nothing hidden.

blocks.alt: Mobile before and after for home, menu, customise and cart

label: User flow
title: One clear path, from craving to collected.
lead: Every route leads to the same single-page checkout. The only fork is when: right now, or booked for later.

blocks.alt: User flow: home, menu, customise, cart and location lead to checkout; then as soon as possible or order ahead; then pay and track

label: Brand
title: Hot. Fresh. Yours.
lead: The promise I designed around. Every screen should feel hot (fast, energetic), fresh (clean, honest) and yours (personal, made your way).

items.title: Bold
items.text: Big type, big photos, one big button.

items.title: Warm
items.text: Talks like a friend at the counter.

items.title: Honest
items.text: Real prices and real times, always.

items.title: Quick
items.text: Nothing between you and pizza.

blocks.alt: Hot. Fresh. Yours. with voice examples: “Ready in about 20 min”, “You save Rs 2,284. Deal applied.” and “That time’s full. Try 7:30?”
Brand system: primary lockup, stacked reversed logo, icon, tile pattern and usage on different backgrounds

label: Visual identity
title: Unmistakably Domino’s, dialled up.
lead: Only the brand’s own colours, the domino tile as a quiet motif, a characterful grotesque for appetite and a calm sans for reading.

blocks.alt: The domino tile, Bricolage Grotesque and Plus Jakarta Sans, and the colour palette

blocks.label: Typography
items: Bricolage Grotesque · headlines and prices
Plus Jakarta Sans · body, labels and UI

label: Art direction
title: Warm photos, friendly people.
lead: Food is shot close and real, never glossy. People are drawn by hand in simple line art, so the brand feels human without stock-photo smiles.

blocks.alt: Close, warm pizza photos next to hand-drawn character illustrations on brand colours
Campaign: “Order at 5. Eat at 7.”, a story, a feed post and app notifications

label: Components
title: A small kit that does a lot.
lead: One strong button for the action that matters, segmented pickers for sizes, honest tags for diet and heat, and one icon set at a single stroke weight.

blocks.alt: Buttons, size picker and tags, time slots, feedback toast and a Lucide icon set

label: Key screens
title: A hero you can order from.
lead: The first screen is a swipeable deck of pizzas with a size picker and a one-tap Add, followed by offers that sell themselves.

blocks.alt: Mobile home with the pizza hero deck and campaign posters

blocks.title: Home
items: Swipe, tap or use the arrow keys
Live price per size, under the photo
Campaign posters inspired by the shopfronts

blocks.alt: Mobile menu with sticky filters and the customise sheet

blocks.title: Filter in a tap, customise in a sheet
items: Veg, Spicy and search always in reach
The pizza photo grows with the size
Running total on the Add button

blocks.alt: Mobile cart with free delivery and the best deal applied

blocks.title: A cart that does the maths
items: Delivery or pickup, switched at the top
Free-delivery progress, no guessing
Taxes included in every price

blocks.alt: Checkout on desktop and mobile with day and time slots

blocks.title: Now, or order ahead
items: Day, then time, grouped by lunch, afternoon, evening and late night
Busy times are marked Full instead of hidden
Change or cancel until 30 minutes before

blocks.alt: Secure payment with a live card preview, and order tracking

blocks.title: Pay the local way, track to the door
items: Cards with 3-D Secure, Genie, eZ Cash, FriMi and LankaQR
The card preview updates as you type
Clear stages from oven to door
Change time or cancel, right from tracking

label: Responsive
title: From a 320px phone to a 4K screen.
lead: The same components reflow across twelve tested screen sizes, with no sideways scrolling anywhere.

blocks.alt: Desktop menu, cart and checkout
Every screen. One clear path.

label: Outcome
title: What the redesign delivers.
lead: A working, responsive prototype that removes the biggest points of friction, ready to test with real customers.

items.title: 1 tap
items.text: To add a pizza, from the hero or any menu card.

items.title: 1 page
items.text: Checkout: details, timing and payment together.

items.title: 7 days
items.text: Order ahead: pickup or delivery, changeable later.
Local ways to pay: cards, Genie, eZ Cash, FriMi, LankaQR.

items.title: 320px up to 4K
items.text: Twelve screen sizes, no sideways scroll.

items.title: AA · WCAG 2.2
items.text: Keyboard, screen reader and reduced motion.

items.title: What I learned
items: Trust is designed in the details. Showing the real price early did more than any visual flourish.

items.title: What I’d test next
items: Usability sessions with customers in Colombo, and the hero deck against a menu-first home.

items.title: What comes after
items: Reorder in one tap, group orders, and loyalty points shown right in the cart.
